   175	    { name: "a real-entropy seed in an untracked file", files: { [`${tag}.txt`]: `seed: ${encodeSeed(randomBytes(16), "ed25519")}\n` }, expect: "FAIL", needle: `${tag}.txt` },
   176	    { name: "an ElGamal secret under docs/reviews", files: { [`docs/reviews/${tag}.md`]: `{"sk": "${randomBytes(32).toString("hex")}"}\n` }, expect: "FAIL", needle: `docs/reviews/${tag}.md` },
   177	    { name: "a stored secret, bare, against a synthetic store", files: { [`${tag}-known.txt`]: `${sk}\n` }, store: { "state.json": JSON.stringify({ x: { sk } }) }, expect: "FAIL", needle: `${tag}-known.txt` },
   178	    { name: "this machine's home path in an evidence README", files: { [`docs/evidence/${tag}/README.md`]: `ran from ${homedir()}/x\n` }, expect: "FAIL", needle: `docs/evidence/${tag}/README.md` },
   179	    { name: "a seed in a gitignored file still PASSES", files: { [`${tag}.log`]: `${encodeSeed(randomBytes(16), "secp256k1")}\n` }, expect: "PASS" },
   180	  ];
   181	}
   182	
   183	function plantRun(p: Plant): Run {
   184	  const written: string[] = [];
   185	  let storeDir: string | undefined;
   186	  try {
   187	    for (const [rel, body] of Object.entries(p.files)) {
   188	      const abs = join(ROOT, rel);
   189	      if (existsSync(abs)) throw new Error(`refusing to overwrite ${rel}`);
   190	      // Remove the shallowest directory this plant creates, or the file itself.
   191	      let created = abs;
   192	      for (let d = dirname(abs); d !== ROOT && !existsSync(d); d = dirname(d)) created = d;
   193	      mkdirSync(dirname(abs), { recursive: true });
   194	      writeFileSync(abs, body);
   195	      written.push(created);
   196	      cleanup.push(created);
   197	    }
   198	    const args = ["--tree-only"];
   199	    if (p.store) {
   200	      storeDir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "break-no-secrets-store-"));
   201	      cleanup.push(storeDir);
   202	      for (const [n, b] of Object.entries(p.store)) writeFileSync(join(storeDir, n), b);
   203	      args.push("--store", storeDir);
   204	    }
   205	    return run(GATE, args);
   206	  } finally {
   207	    for (const w of written) rmSync(w, { recursive: true, force: true });
   208	    if (storeDir) rmSync(storeDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
   209	  }
   210	}
   211	
   212	type Verdict = "TICK" | "NOT-CAUGHT" | "WRONG-CONTROL" | "CRASH" | "DID-NOT-APPLY";
   213	
   214	function judgeMutation(m: Mutation): { v: Verdict; detail: string } {
   215	  const body = mutate(m);
   216	  if (body === null) return { v: "DID-NOT-APPLY", detail: `the edit matched ${SRC.split(m.find).length - 1} times, not once` };
   217	  writeFileSync(MUTANT, body);
   218	  const r = run(MUTANT, m.args ?? ["--controls-only"]);
   219	  if (r.crash) return { v: "CRASH", detail: r.out.slice(-4).join(" | ") };
   220	  if (r.verdict !== (m.expect ?? "CONTROL-FAILED") || r.exit !== 2) return { v: "NOT-CAUGHT", detail: `verdict=${r.verdict} exit=${r.exit}` };
   221	  const lines = failureLines(r);
   222	  if (!lines.some((l) => l.includes(m.needle))) return { v: "WRONG-CONTROL", detail: `failed, but not on '${m.needle}': ${lines.slice(0, 3).join(" | ")}` };
   223	  return { v: "TICK", detail: lines.filter((l) => l.includes(m.needle))[0].trim() };
   224	}
   225	
   226	function judgePlant(p: Plant): { v: Verdict; detail: string } {
   227	  const r = plantRun(p);
   228	  if (r.crash) return { v: "CRASH", detail: r.out.slice(-4).join(" | ") };
   229	  if (p.expect === "PASS") return r.exit === 0 && r.verdict === "PASS" ? { v: "TICK", detail: "PASS" } : { v: "NOT-CAUGHT", detail: `expected PASS, got verdict=${r.verdict} exit=${r.exit}` };
   230	  if (r.verdict !== "FAIL" || r.exit !== 1) return { v: "NOT-CAUGHT", detail: `verdict=${r.verdict} exit=${r.exit}` };
   231	  const lines = failureLines(r);
   232	  if (!lines.some((l) => l.includes(p.needle!))) return { v: "WRONG-CONTROL", detail: `failed, but not naming '${p.needle}'` };
   233	  return { v: "TICK", detail: lines.filter((l) => l.includes(p.needle!))[0].trim() };
   234	}
   235	
   236	function finish(ok: boolean, n: number, bad: number): never {
   237	  console.log(`break-no-secrets-gate: verdict=${ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL"} probes=${n} failed=${bad}`);
   238	  process.exit(ok ? 0 : 1);
   239	}
   240	
   241	if (import.meta.main) {
   242	  const selfTest = process.argv.includes("--self-test");
   243	  let n = 0, bad = 0;
   244	  const report = (name: string, want: Verdict | "REJECTED", got: { v: Verdict; detail: string }) => {
   245	    n++;
   246	    const ok = want === "REJECTED" ? got.v !== "TICK" : got.v === want;
   247	    if (!ok) bad++;
   248	    console.log(`${ok ? "✓" : "✗"} ${name}: ${got.v}${want === "REJECTED" ? " (must be rejected)" : ""} — ${got.detail}`);
   249	  };
   250	
   251	  if (selfTest) {
   252	    // Three probes that must be REJECTED and one that must tick, so a harness
   253	    // that rejects everything cannot pass its own self-test.
   254	    report("self-test: a no-op mutation must not count as caught", "REJECTED", judgeMutation({ name: "no-op", find: "const WINDOW = 40;", replace: "const WINDOW = 40; ", needle: "type annotation" }));
   255	    report("self-test: a crash must be classified CRASH", "REJECTED", judgeMutation({ name: "crash", find: "const WINDOW = 40;", replace: "const WINDOW = ;", needle: "type annotation" }));
   256	    report("self-test: the wrong control's failure must not count", "REJECTED", judgeMutation({ name: "wrong", find: "const WINDOW = 40;", replace: "const WINDOW = 4;", needle: "a GitHub token" }));
   257	    report("self-test: a correct probe must tick", "TICK", judgeMutation(MUTATIONS.find((m) => m.name === "JSON-escaped home rule removed")!));
   258	    finish(bad === 0, n, bad);
   259	  }
   260	
   261	  writeFileSync(MUTANT, SRC);
   262	  const base = run(MUTANT, ["--controls-only"]);
   263	  report("baseline: the unmutated copy passes its controls", "TICK", base.crash ? { v: "CRASH", detail: base.out.slice(-3).join(" | ") } : base.verdict === "CONTROLS-PASS" && base.exit === 0 ? { v: "TICK", detail: base.out.find((l) => l.startsWith("controls:")) ?? "" } : { v: "NOT-CAUGHT", detail: `verdict=${base.verdict}` });
   264	  for (const m of MUTATIONS) report(`mutation: ${m.name}`, "TICK", judgeMutation(m));
   265	  for (const args of CLI_REFUSALS) {
   266	    const r = run(GATE, args);
   267	    report(`cli: ${args.join(" ")} is refused`, "TICK", r.crash ? { v: "CRASH", detail: r.out.slice(-3).join(" | ") } : r.verdict === "REFUSED" && r.exit === 2 ? { v: "TICK", detail: r.out.find((l) => l.startsWith("REFUSED:")) ?? "" } : { v: "NOT-CAUGHT", detail: `verdict=${r.verdict} exit=${r.exit}` });
   268	  }
   269	
   270	  const treeBase = run(GATE, ["--tree-only"]);
   271	  const clean = !treeBase.crash && treeBase.verdict === "PASS" && treeBase.exit === 0;
   272	  report("baseline: the real tree passes before anything is planted", "TICK", clean ? { v: "TICK", detail: "PASS" } : { v: "NOT-CAUGHT", detail: `verdict=${treeBase.verdict} exit=${treeBase.exit}; tree plants cannot be judged against a failing baseline` });
   273	  if (clean) for (const p of plants()) report(`plant: ${p.name}`, "TICK", judgePlant(p));
   274	  else console.log("  (tree plants SKIPPED: a FAIL against a failing baseline proves nothing about the plant)");
   275	  finish(bad === 0, n, bad);
   276	}
     1	/**
     2	 * scrub-personal-data.ts — replace this machine's personal paths, and email
     3	 * addresses the secret sweep does not allow, with placeholders.
     4	 *
     5	 *   bun run tools/scrub-personal-data.ts <file>...            # dry run: counts only
     6	 *   bun run tools/scrub-personal-data.ts --write <file>...    # rewrite in place
     7	 *
     8	 * # Why this exists
     9	 *
    10	 * `make check-no-secrets` fails on a home directory, a macOS per-user temp
    11	 * directory or a personal email address anywhere in what would be published.
    12	 * Review transcripts and build logs pick those up every time a tool prints its
    13	 * working directory, so scrubbing is a repeated task, not a one-off — and a
    14	 * repeated hand edit is how a copy gets missed (`CLAUDE.md`: grep the phrase,
    15	 * not the line).
    16	 *
    17	 * # What it replaces
    18	 *
    19	 * Computed at run time from the machine, so this file names no person:
    20	 *
    21	 * | placeholder | what |
    22	 * |---|---|
    23	 * | `$REPO` | this repository's root, plain or JSON-escaped |
    24	 * | `$REPO_SLUG` | the root dash-encoded, as tools name a directory after a path |
    25	 * | `$HOME` | the home directory, plain or JSON-escaped |
    26	 * | `$HOME_SLUG` | the home directory dash-encoded |
    27	 * | `$USER_TMP` | the macOS per-user temp root under `/var/folders` |
    28	 * | `redacted@example.invalid` | every email address `check-no-secrets.ts` does not allow |
    29	 *
    30	 * ⚠ **Not angle brackets.** The first version wrote `<home>`, and GitHub
    31	 * renders a bare `<home>` in Markdown as an HTML tag and drops it, so a
    32	 * scrubbed path would have read as `/.nvm/...`. Shell-style names render
    33	 * literally and, in a command, are still valid shell.
    34	 *
    35	 * Emails are found by **the gate's own `emailHits()`**, so the two cannot
    36	 * disagree about what an address is. Afterwards the gate's path and email
    37	 * detectors run over the result, and anything the gate would still FAIL on —
    38	 * another user's home under a name that is not generic, say — is printed and the
    39	 * run exits 1, so it is handled by hand rather than left in place.
    40	 *
    41	 * ⚠ **Corrected by `REVIEW-056` S3-4.** This said *"anything left … is
    42	 * printed"*, and two cases contradict that. A home under a generic name such as
    43	 * `/home/user` is allowed by the gate, so it is neither scrubbed nor printed.
    44	 * And this machine's own paths are replaced EVERYWHERE they occur, including
    45	 * where the gate would not flag them, such as glued to a preceding word. That
    46	 * over-reach is deliberate: it only ever removes this machine's paths.
    47	 *
    48	 * # What it will not do
    49	 *
    50	 * * **Edit code.** A path in a `.ts`, `.rs`, `.py`, `.sh` or `.js` file is a
    51	 *   bug to fix, not text to redact: a scrubbed path no longer runs. Those files
    52	 *   are refused unless `--allow-code` is given.
    53	 * * **Print a value.** Counts per rule, per file, only.
    54	 * * **Touch a secret.** Seeds, scalars and credentials are not personal data and
    55	 *   must not be "scrubbed" into a placeholder that hides that they were there.
    56	 *   Rotate or remove those by hand.
    57	 */
    58	
    59	import { readFileSync, realpathSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
    60	import { homedir, tmpdir } from "node:os";
    61	import { join } from "node:path";
    62	import { emailHits, pathHits } from "./check-no-secrets.ts";
    63	
    64	const CODE = /\.(ts|tsx|js|mjs|cjs|rs|py|sh)$/;
    65	
    66	function substitutions(): { rule: string; from: string; to: string }[] {
    67	  const repo = realpathSync(join(import.meta.dir, ".."));
    68	  const home = realpathSync(homedir());
    69	  const subs: { rule: string; from: string; to: string }[] = [];
    70	  const t = realpathSync(tmpdir()).match(/^(\/private)?(\/var\/folders\/[^/]+\/[^/]+)/);
    71	  if (t) {
    72	    subs.push({ rule: "user-tmp", from: "/private" + t[2], to: "$USER_TMP" });
    73	    subs.push({ rule: "user-tmp", from: t[2], to: "$USER_TMP" });
    74	  }
    75	  const esc = (p: string) => p.replaceAll("/", "\\/");
    76	  const dash = (p: string) => p.replaceAll("/", "-");
    77	  subs.push(
    78	    { rule: "repo", from: esc(repo), to: "$REPO" },
    79	    { rule: "repo", from: repo, to: "$REPO" },
    80	    { rule: "repo-slug", from: dash(repo), to: "$REPO_SLUG" },
    81	    { rule: "home", from: esc(home), to: "$HOME" },
    82	    { rule: "home", from: home, to: "$HOME" },
    83	    { rule: "home-slug", from: dash(home) + "-", to: "$HOME_SLUG-" },
    84	  );
    85	  // Longest first, so the repository root wins over the home directory it is under.
    86	  return subs.sort((a, b) => b.from.length - a.from.length);
    87	}
    88	
    89	export function scrub(text: string): { text: string; counts: Map<string, number> } {
    90	  const counts = new Map<string, number>();
    91	  let out = text;
    92	  for (const s of substitutions()) {
    93	    const n = out.split(s.from).length - 1;
    94	    if (n) { counts.set(s.rule, (counts.get(s.rule) ?? 0) + n); out = out.replaceAll(s.from, s.to); }
    95	  }
    96	  const emails = emailHits(out).filter((h) => !h.allowedBy).sort((a, b) => b.at - a.at);
    97	  for (const h of emails) out = out.slice(0, h.at) + "redacted@example.invalid" + out.slice(h.at + h.len!);
    98	  if (emails.length) counts.set("email", emails.length);
    99	  return { text: out, counts };
   100	}

   102	if (import.meta.main) {
   103	  const argv = process.argv.slice(2);
   104	  const write = argv.includes("--write");
   105	  const allowCode = argv.includes("--allow-code");
   106	  const files = argv.filter((a) => !a.startsWith("--"));
   107	  if (!files.length) { console.log("usage: scrub-personal-data.ts [--write] [--allow-code] <file>..."); process.exit(2); }
   108	  let left = 0, changed = 0;
   109	  const total = new Map<string, number>();
   110	  console.log("| file | substitutions |\n|---|---|");
   111	  for (const f of files) {
   112	    if (CODE.test(f) && !allowCode) { console.log(`| \`${f}\` | REFUSED: code file, fix the path by hand |`); left++; continue; }
   113	    const before = readFileSync(f, "latin1");
   114	    const { text, counts } = scrub(before);
   115	    const remaining = [...pathHits(text), ...emailHits(text)].filter((h) => !h.allowedBy);
   116	    if (counts.size) {
   117	      changed++;
   118	      for (const [k, n] of counts) total.set(k, (total.get(k) ?? 0) + n);
   119	      console.log(`| \`${f}\` | ${[...counts].map(([k, n]) => `${k} ${n}`).join(", ")} |`);
   120	      if (write) writeFileSync(f, text, "latin1");
   121	    }
   122	    for (const h of remaining) { left++; console.log(`| \`${f}\` | LEFT: ${h.why} — ${h.shown} |`); }
   123	  }
   124	  console.log(`\n${write ? "rewrote" : "would rewrite"} ${changed} file(s); totals: ${[...total].map(([k, n]) => `${k} ${n}`).join(", ") || "none"}; ${left} item(s) need a hand fix`);
   125	  process.exit(left ? 1 : 0);
   126	}

   319	/**
   320	 * 58 to 66 hex digits, not exactly 64 or 66: a scalar printed without padding
   321	 * drops its leading zero nibbles, one time in sixteen per nibble (`REVIEW-056`
   322	 * S3-1). A label is still required, so a 60-digit hash fragment alone is not hit.
   323	 */
   324	const HEX_SCALAR = /(?<![0-9A-Za-z])(?:0x)?([0-9A-Fa-f]{58,66})(?![0-9A-Za-z])/g;
   325	const HEX_32 = /(?<![0-9A-Za-z])(?:0x)?([0-9A-Fa-f]{32})(?![0-9A-Za-z])/g;
   326	
   327	export function labelledHits(text: string): Hit[] {
   328	  const out: Hit[] = [];
   329	  const pub = publicScalars();
   330	  for (const m of text.matchAll(HEX_SCALAR)) {
   331	    const label = labelNear(text, m.index!, m.index! + m[0].length, SECRET_COMPONENTS);
   332	    if (!label) continue;
   333	    const v = m[1].toLowerCase();
   334	    const toy = BigInt("0x" + v) < TOY_SCALAR_BOUND ? "a toy scalar below 2^32" : undefined;
   335	    // One byte repeated is guessable from 256 candidates, the same argument as the seed rule.
   336	    const repeated = v.length % 2 === 0 && v.match(/../g)!.every((b) => b === v.slice(0, 2)) ? "one byte repeated" : undefined;
   337	    out.push({ cls: "labelled-scalar", at: m.index!, shown: redact(m[1]), why: `${m[1].length} hex digits labelled '${label}'`, allowedBy: pub.get(v) ?? toy ?? repeated });
   338	  }
   339	  for (const m of text.matchAll(HEX_32)) {
   340	    const label = labelNear(text, m.index!, m.index! + m[0].length, ENTROPY_COMPONENTS);
   341	    if (!label) continue;
   342	    const rule = publicEntropyRule(Uint8Array.from(Buffer.from(m[1], "hex")));
   343	    out.push({ cls: "seed-entropy-hex", at: m.index!, shown: redact(m[1]), why: `32 hex digits labelled '${label}'`, allowedBy: rule ? `public entropy: ${rule}` : undefined });
   344	  }
   345	  return out;
   346	}

   348	const ALNUM = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789";
   349	const rnd = (n: number, alphabet = ALNUM) => Array.from(randomBytes(n), (b) => alphabet[b % alphabet.length]).join("");

   351	/**
   352	 * Each pattern carries a SAMPLE, built here at run time so this file contains
   353	 * none, and `runControls()` plants every sample (`REVIEW-056` S1-1: only two of
   354	 * ten patterns had a control, so deleting any other passed every check).
   355	 */
   356	export const CREDENTIALS: { name: string; re: RegExp; sample: () => string }[] = [
   357	  { name: "PEM private key", re: /-----BEGIN (?:[A-Z0-9]+ )*PRIVATE KEY(?: BLOCK)?-----/g, sample: () => "-----BEGIN " + "RSA PRIVATE KEY-----" },
   358	  { name: "GitHub token", re: /\bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}\b/g, sample: () => "gh" + "p_" + rnd(36) },
   359	  { name: "GitHub fine-grained token", re: /\bgithub_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{50,}/g, sample: () => "github" + "_pat_" + rnd(60, ALNUM + "_") },
   360	  { name: "Anthropic API key", re: /\bsk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}/g, sample: () => "sk-" + "ant-" + rnd(40) },
   361	  { name: "OpenAI API key", re: /\bsk-(?:proj-)?[A-Za-z0-9_-]{40,}/g, sample: () => "sk-" + rnd(48) },
   362	  { name: "AWS access key id", re: /\b(?:AKIA|ASIA)[0-9A-Z]{16}\b/g, sample: () => "AK" + "IA" + rnd(16, "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ234567") },
   363	  { name: "AWS secret access key", re: /\baws_?secret_?access_?key["'`\s:=]{1,8}[A-Za-z0-9/+]{40}(?![A-Za-z0-9/+])/gi, sample: () => "aws_secret" + "_access_key = " + rnd(40, ALNUM + "/+") },
   364	  { name: "Slack token", re: /\bxox[abprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}/g, sample: () => "xo" + "xb-" + rnd(24) },
   365	  // ⚠ Not a trailing `\b`: a key may END in `-`, and `\b` after `-` needs a word
   366	  // character next, so one key in 32 was missed. Found as a flaky control.
   367	  { name: "Google API key", re: /\bAIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}(?![0-9A-Za-z_-])/g, sample: () => "AI" + "za" + rnd(35, ALNUM + "_-") },
   368	  { name: "npm token", re: /\bnpm_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}\b/g, sample: () => "np" + "m_" + rnd(36) },
   369	  { name: "GitLab token", re: /\bglpat-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}/g, sample: () => "gl" + "pat-" + rnd(24) },
   370	];
   371	
   372	export function credentialHits(text: string): Hit[] {
   373	  const out: Hit[] = [];
   374	  for (const c of CREDENTIALS) for (const m of text.matchAll(c.re)) {
   375	    // A value ending in sixteen copies of one character is a placeholder, as in
   376	    // `aws_secret_access_key=AAAA…`. A real token does so with negligible probability.
   377	    const tail = m[0].slice(-16);
   378	    const placeholder = c.name !== "PEM private key" && [...tail].every((ch) => ch === tail[0]) ? "a placeholder (its last 16 characters are one character)" : undefined;
   379	    out.push({ cls: "credential", at: m.index!, shown: redact(m[0]), why: c.name, allowedBy: placeholder });
   380	  }
   381	  return out;
   382	}

   384	/**
   385	 * Five encodings of a home directory, because a transcript records paths the
   386	 * way the tool that printed them did: plain, JSON-escaped, URL-encoded,
   387	 * Windows, and the dash-encoded form tools use to name a directory after a
   388	 * path. Measured 2026-10-18: the plain and dash forms were both in the tree.
   389	 */
   390	const NAME = "([A-Za-z0-9._][A-Za-z0-9._-]*)";
   391	const NOT_URL = "(?<![A-Za-z0-9._~%-])";
   392	const PATH_RULES: { rule: string; re: RegExp }[] = [
   393	  { rule: "macOS home", re: new RegExp(`${NOT_URL}/Users/${NAME}`, "g") },
   394	  { rule: "Linux home", re: new RegExp(`${NOT_URL}/home/${NAME}`, "g") },
   395	  { rule: "JSON-escaped home", re: new RegExp(`\\\\/(?:Users|home)\\\\/${NAME}`, "g") },
   396	  { rule: "URL-encoded home", re: new RegExp(`%2[Ff](?:Users|home)%2[Ff]${NAME}`, "g") },
   397	  { rule: "Windows home", re: new RegExp(`[A-Za-z]:\\\\{1,2}Users\\\\{1,2}${NAME}`, "g") },
   398	  { rule: "dash-encoded home", re: /(?<![A-Za-z0-9])-(?:Users|home)-([A-Za-z0-9._]+)-/g },

   400	];
   401	/** User names that identify nobody. Compared case-insensitively. */
   402	export const GENERIC_USERS = new Set(["runner", "user", "username", "you", "yourname", "me", "name", "example", "shared", "alice", "bob"]);
   403	
   404	export function pathHits(text: string): Hit[] {
   405	  const out: Hit[] = [];
   406	  for (const { rule, re } of PATH_RULES) {
   407	    for (const m of text.matchAll(re)) {
   408	      const who = m[1];
   409	      const generic = rule !== "macOS per-user temp" && GENERIC_USERS.has(who.toLowerCase());
   410	      out.push({ cls: "personal-path", at: m.index!, len: m[0].length, shown: `${rule}: ${redact(who)}`, why: rule, allowedBy: generic ? "generic user name" : undefined });
   411	    }
   412	  }
   413	  return out;
   414	}
   415	
   416	/** RFC 2606 / RFC 6761 reserved names, plus three role addresses. */
   417	const RESERVED_TLDS = new Set(["example", "invalid", "test", "localhost"]);
   418	const RESERVED_DOMAINS = new Set(["example.com", "example.org", "example.net"]);
   419	export const ROLE_ADDRESSES = new Set(["noreply@github.com", "noreply@anthropic.com", "git@github.com"]);
   420	
   421	const isLocalChar = (c: number) =>
   422	  (c >= 48 && c <= 57) || (c >= 65 && c <= 90) || (c >= 97 && c <= 122) || c === 46 || c === 95 || c === 37 || c === 43 || c === 45;
   423	const isDomainChar = (c: number) => (c >= 48 && c <= 57) || (c >= 65 && c <= 90) || (c >= 97 && c <= 122) || c === 46 || c === 45;
   424	
   425	/**
   426	 * Scans for `@` and expands outward, rather than one regex, because
   427	 * `[local-chars]+@` backtracks quadratically over a long run with no `@`.
   428	 */
   429	export function emailHits(text: string): Hit[] {
   430	  const out: Hit[] = [];
   431	  for (let i = text.indexOf("@"); i !== -1; i = text.indexOf("@", i + 1)) {
   432	    let s = i;
   433	    while (s > 0 && i - s < 64 && isLocalChar(text.charCodeAt(s - 1))) s--;
   434	    let e = i + 1;
   435	    while (e < text.length && e - i < 254 && isDomainChar(text.charCodeAt(e))) e++;
   436	    const local = text.slice(s, i).replace(/^\.+/, "");
   437	    const domain = text.slice(i + 1, e).replace(/\.+$/, "").toLowerCase();
   438	    if (!local || !/^[a-z0-9-]+(\.[a-z0-9-]+)*\.[a-z]{2,}$/.test(domain)) continue;
   439	    const addr = `${local.toLowerCase()}@${domain}`;
   440	    const tld = domain.slice(domain.lastIndexOf(".") + 1);
   441	    const allowed = ROLE_ADDRESSES.has(addr)
   442	      ? "role address"
   443	      : RESERVED_TLDS.has(tld) || [...RESERVED_DOMAINS].some((d) => domain === d || domain.endsWith("." + d))
   444	        ? "reserved domain"
   445	        : undefined;
   446	    out.push({ cls: "email", at: i - local.length, len: local.length + 1 + domain.length, shown: `${local[0]}…@${domain}`, why: "email address", allowedBy: allowed });
   447	  }
   448	  return out;
   449	}
   450	
   451	const SECRET_FILE = /(^|\/)(state\.json|facility-state\.json|facility-book\.json|profile\.json|\.env(\.(?!example$|sample$)[^/]+)?|[^/]*\.(seed|secret|pem|key|p12|pfx|jks|keystore)|id_(rsa|dsa|ecdsa|ed25519)|\.npmrc|\.netrc|credentials(\.json)?)$/i;
   452	
   453	export function secretFileHit(path: string): Hit | null {
   454	  return SECRET_FILE.test(path) ? { cls: "secret-file", at: 0, shown: path, why: "named like a secret store or a key file" } : null;
   455	}

   457	// ------------------------------------------------------- the known-value class
   458	
   459	export interface Needle { value: string; label: string; kind: "hex" | "b58" }
   460	
   461	/**
   462	 * Every encoding of a stored seed this gate can see: the seed, its entropy, the
   463	 * ElGamal key the ruled derivation gives it, and its XRPL signing key with and
   464	 * without the algorithm prefix. ⚠ **The derived key matters most**: a holder
   465	 * under `derived-from-master-seed` has NO ElGamal secret in any file, so a
   466	 * check over stored values alone would never see it.
   467	 */
   468	export function needlesForSeed(seed: string, label: string): Needle[] {
   469	  const d = decodeSeedLike(seed)!;
   470	  const priv = deriveKeypair(seed).privateKey.toLowerCase();
   471	  return [
   472	    { value: seed, label: `${label} (as stored)`, kind: "b58" },
   473	    { value: hex(d.entropy), label: `${label} (entropy, hex)`, kind: "hex" },
   474	    { value: deriveElGamalKey(seed).sk.toLowerCase(), label: `${label} (ElGamal key derived from it)`, kind: "hex" },
   475	    { value: priv, label: `${label} (signing key)`, kind: "hex" },
   476	    { value: priv.slice(2), label: `${label} (signing key, no prefix)`, kind: "hex" },
   477	  ];
   478	}
   479	
   480	export interface Store { files: string[]; needles: Needle[]; secrets: number; publicSkipped: number }
   481	
   482	/** Default places the project keeps secrets. `rebuild-env.sh` and `facility/` write these. */
   483	export function defaultStorePaths(): string[] {
   484	  const p = [join(homedir(), ".wconf"), "/tmp/wconf"];
   485	  if (process.env.WCONF_STATE_BACKUP) p.unshift(process.env.WCONF_STATE_BACKUP);
   486	  return p;
   487	}
   488	
   489	export function loadStore(paths: string[], env: Record<string, string | undefined> = process.env): Store {
   490	  const st: Store = { files: [], needles: [], secrets: 0, publicSkipped: 0 };
   491	  const files: string[] = [];
   492	  for (const p of paths) {
   493	    if (!existsSync(p)) continue;
   494	    const s = lstatSync(p);
   495	    if (s.isFile()) files.push(p);
   496	    else if (s.isDirectory()) for (const n of readdirSync(p)) if (n.includes(".json") && lstatSync(join(p, n)).isFile()) files.push(join(p, n));
   497	  }
   498	  // Counted by distinct VALUE: the same seed in two copies of state.json is one
   499	  // secret, and a count that doubled it would claim coverage it does not have.
   500	  const seen = new Set<string>();
   501	  const addSeed = (seed: string, label: string) => {
   502	    const d = decodeSeedLike(seed);
   503	    if (!d || !d.checksumOk) return;
   504	    if (publicEntropyRule(d.entropy)) { st.publicSkipped++; return; }
   505	    if (seen.has(seed)) return;
   506	    seen.add(seed);
   507	    st.secrets++;
   508	    st.needles.push(...needlesForSeed(seed, label));
   509	  };
   510	  const addHex = (v: string, label: string) => {
   511	    const k = v.toLowerCase();
   512	    if (seen.has(k)) return;
   513	    seen.add(k);
   514	    st.secrets++;
   515	    st.needles.push({ value: k, label, kind: "hex" });
   516	  };
   517	  for (const f of files) {
   518	    st.files.push(f);
   519	    const raw = readFileSync(f, "utf8");
   520	    const name = f.slice(f.lastIndexOf("/") + 1);
   521	    let json: unknown;
   522	    // ⚠ A malformed store file REFUSES (`REVIEW-056` S3-3). It used to fall back
   523	    // to scanning the raw text for seeds, which silently dropped every 64-hex
   524	    // scalar in it — the one shape only this class can find — while another
   525	    // file kept the store non-empty, so no refusal fired.
   526	    try { json = JSON.parse(raw); } catch (e) {
   527	      throw new Error(`store file ${f} is not valid JSON (${String(e).slice(0, 80)}); the known-value class cannot tell its secrets from its hashes, so it refuses rather than guess`);
   528	    }
   529	    const walk = (o: unknown, path: string) => {
   530	      if (Array.isArray(o)) o.forEach((v, i) => walk(v, `${path}[${i}]`));
   531	      else if (o && typeof o === "object") for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(o)) walk(v, `${path}.${k}`);
   532	      else if (typeof o === "string") {
   533	        const key = path.slice(path.lastIndexOf(".") + 1).replace(/\[\d+\]$/, "");
   534	        if (decodeSeedLike(o)?.checksumOk) addSeed(o, `${name}:${path}`);
   535	        else if (/^[0-9A-Fa-f]{64}$/.test(o) && components(key).some((c) => SECRET_COMPONENTS.has(c))) addHex(o, `${name}:${path}`);
   536	      }
   537	    };
   538	    walk(json, "");
   539	  }
   540	  const envSk = env.WCONF_ELGAMAL_SK?.trim();
   541	  if (envSk && /^[0-9A-Fa-f]{64}$/.test(envSk)) addHex(envSk, "environment: WCONF_ELGAMAL_SK");
   542	  return st;
   543	}
   544	
   545	const HEXRUN = /[0-9A-Fa-f]{32,}/g;
   546	export function knownHits(text: string, store: Store): Hit[] {
   547	  if (!store.needles.length) return [];
   548	  const out: Hit[] = [];
   549	  const hexN = store.needles.filter((n) => n.kind === "hex");
   550	  const b58N = store.needles.filter((n) => n.kind === "b58");
   551	  for (const m of text.matchAll(HEXRUN)) {
   552	    const run = m[0].toLowerCase();
   553	    for (const n of hexN) {
   554	      const k = run.indexOf(n.value);
   555	      if (k !== -1) out.push({ cls: "known-value", at: m.index! + k, shown: n.label, why: "a value from the local secret store" });
   556	    }
   557	  }
   558	  if (b58N.length) {
   559	    for (const m of text.matchAll(B58RUN)) {
   560	      for (const n of b58N) {
   561	        const k = m[0].indexOf(n.value);
   562	        if (k !== -1) out.push({ cls: "known-value", at: m.index! + k, shown: n.label, why: "a value from the local secret store" });
   563	      }
   564	    }
   565	  }
   566	  return out;
   567	}
   568	
   569	/** The one function every scan and every control calls. */
   570	export function scanText(text: string, store: Store): Hit[] {
   571	  return [
   572	    ...seedHits(text), ...labelledHits(text), ...credentialHits(text),
   573	    ...pathHits(text), ...emailHits(text), ...knownHits(text, store),
   574	  ];
   575	}

   578	
   579	/**
   580	 * ⚠ **Every git call ignores replacement objects** (`REVIEW-056` S2-2). By
   581	 * default `cat-file` and `rev-list` silently substitute any object named under
   582	 * `refs/replace/`, so a local replacement could show this gate harmless bytes
   583	 * while a push publishes the original.
   584	 */
   585	const GIT_ENV: Record<string, string> = { GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS: "1" };
   586	
   587	function git(repo: string, args: string[], input?: Uint8Array, env?: Record<string, string>): Uint8Array {
   588	  const r = Bun.spawnSync(["git", "-C", repo, ...args], { stdin: input, stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe", env: { ...process.env, ...GIT_ENV, ...(env ?? {}) } });
   589	  if (r.exitCode !== 0) throw new Error(`git ${args.join(" ")} failed: ${new TextDecoder().decode(r.stderr).trim()}`);
   590	  return r.stdout;
   591	}
   592	const gitText = (repo: string, args: string[], input?: string) => new TextDecoder().decode(git(repo, args, input === undefined ? undefined : new TextEncoder().encode(input)));
   593	
   594	/** Bytes as latin1, so every byte is one character and nothing is replaced. */
   595	const asText = (b: Uint8Array) => Buffer.from(b.buffer, b.byteOffset, b.byteLength).toString("latin1");
   596	
   597	export interface Unit {
   598	  where: string; text: string; scope: "tree" | "history"; kind: "file" | "message" | "path";
   599	  /** How many published paths carry this content; a file count counts these, not blobs. */
   600	  paths?: number;

 succeeded in 0ms:
   601	}
   602	
   603	function* batchObjects(repo: string, shas: string[]): Generator<{ sha: string; type: string; body: Uint8Array }> {
   604	  if (!shas.length) return;
   605	  const out = git(repo, ["cat-file", "--batch"], new TextEncoder().encode(shas.join("\n") + "\n"));
   606	  let i = 0;
   607	  const dec = new TextDecoder();
   608	  while (i < out.length) {
   609	    const nl = out.indexOf(10, i);
   610	    const [sha, type, size] = dec.decode(out.subarray(i, nl)).split(" ");
   611	    if (type === "missing") throw new Error(`object ${sha} missing`);
   612	    const n = Number(size);
   613	    yield { sha, type, body: out.subarray(nl + 1, nl + 1 + n) };
   614	    i = nl + 1 + n + 1;
   615	  }
   616	}
   617	
   618	/**
   619	 * ⚠ **Refuse what this gate cannot read as published** (`REVIEW-056` S2-1, S2-4).
   620	 * A `filter` attribute means `git add` stores bytes a clean filter produced, or,
   621	 * for Git LFS, a pointer while the content is published elsewhere. A
   622	 * `working-tree-encoding` attribute re-encodes on the way in. A gitlink or a
   623	 * nested repository publishes none of its content here. In each case the bytes
   624	 * on disk are not the bytes published, so the gate refuses rather than scanning
   625	 * the wrong ones. `git check-attr` reads `.gitattributes`, `.git/info/attributes`
   626	 * and `core.attributesFile` alike.
   627	 */
   628	function refuseTransformedTree(repo: string, paths: string[], gitlinks: string[]): void {
   629	  if (gitlinks.length) throw new Error(`a submodule or nested repository at ${gitlinks.slice(0, 5).join(", ")}: its content is another repository and is not scanned`);
   630	  if (!paths.length) return;
   631	  const out = gitText(repo, ["check-attr", "-z", "--stdin", "filter", "working-tree-encoding"], paths.join("\0") + "\0").split("\0");
   632	  const bad: string[] = [];
   633	  for (let i = 0; i + 2 < out.length; i += 3) if (out[i + 2] !== "unspecified" && out[i + 2] !== "unset") bad.push(`${out[i]} (${out[i + 1]}=${out[i + 2]})`);
   634	  if (bad.length) throw new Error(`content-transforming attributes on ${bad.length} path(s), e.g. ${bad.slice(0, 3).join(", ")}: the published bytes are not the bytes on disk`);
   635	}
   636	
   637	/** What `git add -A` would commit, read from disk. Symlinks are not followed. */
   638	export function treeUnits(repo: string): Unit[] {
   639	  const names = gitText(repo, ["ls-files", "-z", "--cached", "--others", "--exclude-standard"]).split("\0").filter(Boolean);
   640	  const staged = gitText(repo, ["ls-files", "-z", "-s"]).split("\0").filter(Boolean);
   641	  const gitlinks = staged.filter((l) => l.startsWith("160000 ")).map((l) => l.slice(l.indexOf("\t") + 1));
   642	  // An untracked nested repository is listed as a directory: `git add -A` would record a gitlink.
   643	  gitlinks.push(...names.filter((n) => n.endsWith("/")));
   644	  refuseTransformedTree(repo, names.filter((n) => !n.endsWith("/")), gitlinks);
   645	  const units: Unit[] = [];
   646	  for (const n of [...new Set(names)]) {
   647	    const p = join(repo, n);
   648	    units.push({ where: n, text: n, scope: "tree", kind: "path" });
   649	    if (!existsSync(p) && !lstatSync(p, { throwIfNoEntry: false })) {
   650	      // Deleted on disk, still in the index: the index copy is what a plain commit publishes.
   651	      try { units.push({ where: n, text: asText(git(repo, ["cat-file", "blob", `:${n}`])), scope: "tree", kind: "file" }); } catch { /* not in index either */ }
   652	      continue;
   653	    }
   654	    const s = lstatSync(p);
   655	    if (s.isSymbolicLink()) units.push({ where: `${n} (symlink target)`, text: readlinkSync(p), scope: "tree", kind: "file" });
   656	    else if (s.isFile()) units.push({ where: n, text: asText(readFileSync(p)), scope: "tree", kind: "file" });
   657	  }
   658	  return units;
   659	}
   660	
   661	/** Exactly the blobs of one commit's tree. */
   662	export function revUnits(repo: string, rev: string): Unit[] {
   663	  // ⚠ Split at the FIRST tab only: a path may itself contain one (REVIEW-056 S2-3).
   664	  const entries = gitText(repo, ["ls-tree", "-r", "-z", "--full-tree", rev]).split("\0").filter(Boolean).map((l) => {
   665	    const t = l.indexOf("\t");
   666	    const [mode, type, sha] = l.slice(0, t).split(" ");
   667	    return { mode, type, sha, path: l.slice(t + 1) };
   668	  });
   669	  const gitlinks = entries.filter((e) => e.type === "commit").map((e) => e.path);
   670	  if (gitlinks.length) throw new Error(`a submodule at ${gitlinks.slice(0, 5).join(", ")}: its content is another repository and is not scanned`);
   671	  const blobs = entries.filter((e) => e.type === "blob");
   672	  const pathsOf = new Map<string, string[]>();
   673	  for (const e of blobs) pathsOf.set(e.sha, [...(pathsOf.get(e.sha) ?? []), e.path]);
   674	  const units: Unit[] = blobs.map((e) => ({ where: e.path, text: e.path, scope: "tree" as const, kind: "path" as const }));
   675	  for (const o of batchObjects(repo, [...pathsOf.keys()])) {
   676	    const ps = pathsOf.get(o.sha)!;
   677	    const text = asText(o.body);
   678	    if (ps.some((p) => p === ".gitattributes" || p.endsWith("/.gitattributes")) && /\bfilter\s*=|working-tree-encoding/.test(text)) {
   679	      throw new Error(`content-transforming attributes in ${ps.join(", ")} at ${rev}: the published bytes may not be the blobs`);
   680	    }
   681	    units.push({ where: ps.join("; "), text, scope: "tree", kind: "file", paths: ps.length });
   682	  }
   683	  return units;
   684	}
   685	
   686	/** A commit or tag message, without the identity and signature headers. */
   687	function messageOf(body: Uint8Array): string {
   688	  const t = asText(body);
   689	  const split = t.indexOf("\n\n");
   690	  const head = split === -1 ? t : t.slice(0, split);
   691	  const msg = split === -1 ? "" : t.slice(split + 2);
   692	  // Keep header lines that are not identity or signature: none carry free text
   693	  // except `encoding`, so only the message is returned.
   694	  void head;
   695	  return msg;
   696	}
   697	
   698	export function historyUnits(repo: string): Unit[] {
   699	  // ⚠ A shallow clone or a grafts file hides history from rev-list, so a pass
   700	  // over it would not be a pass over what the repository holds.
   701	  if (gitText(repo, ["rev-parse", "--is-shallow-repository"]).trim() === "true") throw new Error("the repository is shallow; history mode needs every commit");
   702	  const grafts = gitText(repo, ["rev-parse", "--git-path", "info/grafts"]).trim();
   703	  if (existsSync(join(repo, grafts)) || existsSync(grafts)) throw new Error(`a grafts file exists at ${grafts}; it rewrites what rev-list sees`);
   704	  const lines = gitText(repo, ["rev-list", "--objects", "--all"]).split("\n").filter(Boolean);
   705	  const pathOf = new Map<string, string>();
   706	  for (const l of lines) {
   707	    const sp = l.indexOf(" ");
   708	    const sha = sp === -1 ? l : l.slice(0, sp);
   709	    if (!pathOf.has(sha)) pathOf.set(sha, sp === -1 ? "" : l.slice(sp + 1));
   710	  }
   711	  const tags = gitText(repo, ["for-each-ref", "--format=%(objectname) %(objecttype)", "refs/tags"]).split("\n").filter((l) => l.endsWith(" tag")).map((l) => l.split(" ")[0]);
   712	  const units: Unit[] = [];
   713	  for (const o of batchObjects(repo, [...pathOf.keys(), ...tags])) {
   714	    const p = pathOf.get(o.sha) ?? "";
   715	    if (o.type === "blob") units.push({ where: `${p} @ blob ${o.sha.slice(0, 10)}`, text: asText(o.body), scope: "history", kind: "file" });
   716	    else if (o.type === "commit" || o.type === "tag") units.push({ where: `${o.type} ${o.sha.slice(0, 10)} message`, text: messageOf(o.body), scope: "history", kind: "message" });
   717	  }
   718	  // NUL-separated, because a path may contain a tab or a newline (REVIEW-056 S2-3).
   719	  const paths = new Set(gitText(repo, ["log", "--all", "-m", "--format=", "--name-only", "--no-renames", "-z"]).split("\0").filter(Boolean));
   720	  for (const p of paths) units.push({ where: `${p} (a path some commit touched)`, text: p, scope: "history", kind: "path" });
   721	  return units;
   722	}
   723	
   724	export interface Finding extends Hit { where: string; line: number; scope: "tree" | "history" }
   725	
   726	export function scanUnits(units: Unit[], store: Store): { findings: Finding[]; allowed: Map<string, number>; seenAllowed: Set<string> } {
   727	  const findings: Finding[] = [];
   728	  const allowed = new Map<string, number>();
   729	  const seenAllowed = new Set<string>();
   730	  for (const u of units) {
   731	    const hits = u.kind === "path" ? [secretFileHit(u.text), ...pathHits(u.text), ...emailHits(u.text)].filter((h): h is Hit => !!h) : scanText(u.text, store);
   732	    for (const h of hits) {
   733	      if (h.allowedBy) {
   734	        const k = `${h.cls}: ${h.allowedBy}`;
   735	        allowed.set(k, (allowed.get(k) ?? 0) + 1);
   736	        seenAllowed.add(h.allowedBy);
   737	        continue;
   738	      }
   739	      const line = u.kind === "path" ? 0 : u.text.slice(0, h.at).split("\n").length;
   740	      findings.push({ ...h, where: u.where, line, scope: u.scope });
   741	    }
   742	  }
   743	  return { findings, allowed, seenAllowed };
   744	}

   746	// ------------------------------------------------------------------ controls
   747	
   748	/**
   749	 * ⚠⚠ **What this gate cannot see.** Each entry is also an ASSERTED-UNCAUGHT
   750	 * control in `runControls()`: the planted secret must NOT be found. If a later
   751	 * change starts finding one, the control fails and this list must be updated,
   752	 * so the disclosure cannot go stale.
   753	 */
   754	export const LIMITS: string[] = [
   755	  "a secret split across two string literals or two lines",
   756	  "a secret in UTF-16, base64, gzip or any other re-encoding",
   757	  "an unlabelled 64-hex ElGamal secret that is NOT in the local store (no shape rule can tell it from a hash)",
   758	  "a seed or key in RFC 1751 words, or as a decimal or byte array",
   759	  "a home path under a user name on the generic list, which includes alice and bob",
   760	  "a secret listed as an array element under a label, rather than as the value of a key",
   761	  "gitignored files, the reflog and unreachable objects: none of them is published",
   762	  "a hostname, a machine serial, or a person's name — only paths and email addresses are personal-data classes",
   763	];
   764	
   765	let controlsRun = 0;
   766	let controlsFailed: string[] = [];
   767	function control(name: string, ok: boolean, detail = "") {
   768	  controlsRun++;
   769	  if (!ok) controlsFailed.push(`${name}${detail ? ` — ${detail}` : ""}`);
   770	}
   771	
   772	const randName = () => "u" + randomBytes(5).toString("hex");
   773	const realSeed = (type: SeedType) => encodeSeed(randomBytes(16), type);
   774	
   775	/**
   776	 * Builds a throwaway repository with planted secrets and runs the REAL
   777	 * `scanRepo()` over it in tree mode and in history mode. The planted values are

     1	/**
     2	 * break-no-secrets-gate.ts — verify `check-no-secrets` by BREAKING it.
     3	 *
     4	 *   bun run tools/break-no-secrets-gate.ts              # every probe
     5	 *   bun run tools/break-no-secrets-gate.ts --self-test  # verify this harness
     6	 *
     7	 * # Why this exists
     8	 *
     9	 * A gate that has never been broken is a claim. This repository recorded four
    10	 * gates that reported PASS while the thing they checked was broken (`CLAIMS.md`
    11	 * E-165, E-168, E-182, E-201), and each was found by mutating, not by reading.
    12	 * So the mutations are committed and the next session re-runs them.
    13	 *
    14	 * # Three kinds of probe
    15	 *
    16	 * * **Detector mutations.** A copy of the gate with ONE exact edit, written
    17	 *   beside it as `tools/.mutant-<pid>.ts` (gitignored) so its imports resolve,
    18	 *   run with `--controls-only`. It must end `CONTROL-FAILED exit=2`, and the
    19	 *   control the probe names must appear in a `CONTROL FAILED:` line. The real
    20	 *   gate file is never edited, so nothing needs restoring.
    21	 * * **Tree plants.** An untracked file carrying a SYNTHETIC secret is written
    22	 *   into the real tree, and the real gate runs over the real tree. It must end
    23	 *   `FAIL exit=1` with the planted path in the `FAILING` section. ⚠ **A plant
    24	 *   into a gitignored path must still PASS**, because ignored files are not
    25	 *   published. ⚠ **These need a clean baseline**: the unplanted tree must PASS
    26	 *   first, or a FAIL proves nothing about the plant.
    27	 * * **Baselines.** The unmutated copy must end `CONTROLS-PASS exit=0`, so a
    28	 *   harness that rejects everything cannot score full marks.
    29	 *
    30	 * # How a run is classified
    31	 *
    32	 * By the gate's verdict line, which must be the LAST line and must agree with
    33	 * the exit code. Bun exits 1 on a syntax error or an uncaught throw, the same
    34	 * code as a real finding, so the exit code alone cannot tell them apart
    35	 * (`CLAIMS.md` E-259). Anything else is `CRASH`. ⚠ The needle is searched only
    36	 * in the lines that report a failure, never the whole output: the gate prints
    37	 * its control names, so an unscoped search matches every run.
    38	 *
    39	 * ⚠ Tree plants write files into the working tree for a few seconds each. The
    40	 * values are generated here and are not anyone's secret, but do not run
    41	 * `git add -A` while this runs.
    42	 */

    60	interface Run { verdict: string; exit: number; out: string[]; crash: boolean }
    61	function run(file: string, args: string[]): Run {
    62	  const r = Bun.spawnSync(["bun", "run", file, ...args], { cwd: ROOT, stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
    63	  const out = new TextDecoder().decode(r.stdout).split("\n").filter((l) => l.length);
    64	  const last = out[out.length - 1] ?? "";
    65	  const m = last.match(/^check-no-secrets: verdict=(\S+) exit=(\d+)$/);
    66	  const crash = !m || Number(m[2]) !== r.exitCode;
    67	  if (crash) out.push(...new TextDecoder().decode(r.stderr).split("\n").slice(-8).map((l) => `stderr: ${l}`));
    68	  return { verdict: m?.[1] ?? "none", exit: r.exitCode ?? -1, out, crash };
    69	}
    70	
    71	/** Lines that report a failure, and only those. */
    72	function failureLines(r: Run): string[] {
    73	  const control = r.out.filter((l) => l.startsWith("  CONTROL FAILED:") || l.startsWith("  STALE CITED VECTOR:"));
    74	  const i = r.out.findIndex((l) => l.startsWith("FAILING:"));
    75	  if (i === -1) return control;
    76	  const end = r.out.findIndex((l, k) => k > i && (l.startsWith("REPORTED") || l.startsWith("What this gate")));
    77	  return [...control, ...r.out.slice(i, end === -1 ? undefined : end)];
    78	}

    84	  const n = SRC.split(m.find).length - 1;
    85	  return n === 1 ? SRC.replace(m.find, m.replace) : null;
    86	}

  1052	export interface ScanResult { findings: Finding[]; allowed: Map<string, number>; seenAllowed: Set<string>; unitsTree: number; unitsHistory: number }
  1053	
  1054	export function scanRepo(repo: string, store: Store, o: { tree: boolean; history: boolean; rev?: string }): ScanResult {
  1055	  const t = o.tree ? (o.rev ? revUnits(repo, o.rev) : treeUnits(repo)) : [];
  1056	  const h = o.history ? historyUnits(repo) : [];
  1057	  const r = scanUnits([...t, ...h], store);
  1058	  // ⚠ Files are counted by PATH, not by unique blob (REVIEW-056 S5-3): two paths
  1059	  // with identical content are two published files.
  1060	  const files = (us: Unit[]) => us.filter((u) => u.kind === "file").reduce((n, u) => n + (u.paths ?? 1), 0);
  1061	  return { ...r, unitsTree: files(t), unitsHistory: h.filter((u) => u.kind !== "path").length };
  1062	}
  1063	
  1064	interface DecideIn { findings: Finding[]; store: Store; requireStore: boolean; strictHistory: boolean; unitsTree: number; unitsHistory: number; tree: boolean; history: boolean }
  1065	
  1066	export function decide(d: DecideIn): { exit: 0 | 1 | 2; word: string; failing: Finding[]; reported: Finding[]; why?: string } {
  1067	  if (d.requireStore && d.store.secrets === 0) return { exit: 2, word: "REFUSED", failing: [], reported: [], why: "no local secret store found; the known-value class cannot run (pass --no-local-store for the shape classes only)" };
  1068	  if (!d.tree && !d.history) return { exit: 2, word: "REFUSED", failing: [], reported: [], why: "nothing was selected to scan" };
  1069	  if ((d.tree && d.unitsTree === 0) || (d.history && d.unitsHistory === 0)) return { exit: 2, word: "REFUSED", failing: [], reported: [], why: "zero files scanned; an empty scan is not a pass" };
  1070	  const failing = d.findings.filter((f) => f.scope === "tree" || d.strictHistory || !PERSONAL.has(f.cls));
  1071	  const reported = d.findings.filter((f) => !failing.includes(f));
  1072	  if (failing.length) return { exit: 1, word: "FAIL", failing, reported };
  1073	  return { exit: 0, word: d.requireStore ? "PASS" : "PASS-SHAPES-ONLY", failing, reported };
  1074	}

  1076	function printLimits() {
  1077	  console.log("\nWhat this gate does NOT catch (each is an asserted-uncaught control):");
  1078	  for (const l of LIMITS) console.log(`  - ${l}`);
  1079	}

  1081	function printFindings(title: string, fs: Finding[], cap = 25) {
  1082	  if (!fs.length) return;
  1083	  console.log(`\n${title}: ${fs.length}`);
  1084	  const byCls = new Map<Cls, Finding[]>();
  1085	  for (const f of fs) byCls.set(f.cls, [...(byCls.get(f.cls) ?? []), f]);
  1086	  for (const [cls, list] of byCls) {
  1087	    const files = new Map<string, number>();
  1088	    for (const f of list) files.set(f.where, (files.get(f.where) ?? 0) + 1);
  1089	    console.log(`  ${cls}: ${list.length} in ${files.size} location(s)`);
  1090	    for (const f of list.slice(0, cap)) console.log(`    ${f.where}${f.line ? `:${f.line}` : ""}  ${f.why} — ${f.shown}`);
  1091	    if (list.length > cap) console.log(`    … ${list.length - cap} more; per location:`), [...files].slice(0, 60).forEach(([w, n]) => console.log(`      ${n}  ${w}`));
  1092	  }
  1093	}

  1097	/**
  1098	 * Parse the command line STRICTLY (`REVIEW-056` S5-1). An unknown flag, a
  1099	 * missing value or a contradictory pair is refused: a misspelled
  1100	 * `--strict-histroy` used to be ignored and the run reported a pass.
  1101	 */
  1102	export function parseArgs(argv: string[]): { flags: Set<string>; repo?: string; rev?: string; stores: string[] } {
  1103	  const FLAGS = new Set(["--no-local-store", "--history-only", "--tree-only", "--strict-history", "--controls-only"]);
  1104	  const OPTS = new Set(["--repo", "--rev", "--store"]);
  1105	  const flags = new Set<string>();
  1106	  const out: { flags: Set<string>; repo?: string; rev?: string; stores: string[] } = { flags, stores: [] };
  1107	  for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i++) {
  1108	    const a = argv[i];
  1109	    if (FLAGS.has(a)) { flags.add(a); continue; }
  1110	    if (!OPTS.has(a)) throw new Error(`unknown argument '${a}'`);
  1111	    const v = argv[++i];
  1112	    if (v === undefined || v.startsWith("--")) throw new Error(`${a} needs a value`);
  1113	    if (a === "--store") out.stores.push(v);
  1114	    else if (a === "--repo") out.repo = v;
  1115	    else out.rev = v;
  1116	  }

  1097	/**
  1098	 * Parse the command line STRICTLY (`REVIEW-056` S5-1). An unknown flag, a
  1099	 * missing value or a contradictory pair is refused: a misspelled
  1100	 * `--strict-histroy` used to be ignored and the run reported a pass.
  1101	 */
  1102	export function parseArgs(argv: string[]): { flags: Set<string>; repo?: string; rev?: string; stores: string[] } {
  1103	  const FLAGS = new Set(["--no-local-store", "--history-only", "--tree-only", "--strict-history", "--controls-only"]);
  1104	  const OPTS = new Set(["--repo", "--rev", "--store"]);
  1105	  const flags = new Set<string>();
  1106	  const out: { flags: Set<string>; repo?: string; rev?: string; stores: string[] } = { flags, stores: [] };
  1107	  for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i++) {
  1108	    const a = argv[i];
  1109	    if (FLAGS.has(a)) { flags.add(a); continue; }
  1110	    if (!OPTS.has(a)) throw new Error(`unknown argument '${a}'`);
  1111	    const v = argv[++i];
  1112	    if (v === undefined || v.startsWith("--")) throw new Error(`${a} needs a value`);
  1113	    if (a === "--store") out.stores.push(v);
  1114	    else if (a === "--repo") out.repo = v;
  1115	    else out.rev = v;
  1116	  }
  1117	  if (flags.has("--tree-only") && flags.has("--history-only")) throw new Error("--tree-only and --history-only together select nothing");
  1118	  if (out.rev && flags.has("--history-only")) throw new Error("--rev scans one tree; it cannot be combined with --history-only");
  1119	  if (flags.has("--strict-history") && (out.rev || flags.has("--tree-only"))) throw new Error("--strict-history has no effect without a history scan");
  1120	  if (flags.has("--no-local-store") && out.stores.length) throw new Error("--no-local-store and --store contradict each other");
  1121	  return out;
  1122	}

   637	/** What `git add -A` would commit, read from disk. Symlinks are not followed. */
   638	export function treeUnits(repo: string): Unit[] {
   639	  const names = gitText(repo, ["ls-files", "-z", "--cached", "--others", "--exclude-standard"]).split("\0").filter(Boolean);
   640	  const staged = gitText(repo, ["ls-files", "-z", "-s"]).split("\0").filter(Boolean);
   641	  const gitlinks = staged.filter((l) => l.startsWith("160000 ")).map((l) => l.slice(l.indexOf("\t") + 1));
   642	  // An untracked nested repository is listed as a directory: `git add -A` would record a gitlink.
   643	  gitlinks.push(...names.filter((n) => n.endsWith("/")));
   644	  refuseTransformedTree(repo, names.filter((n) => !n.endsWith("/")), gitlinks);
   645	  const units: Unit[] = [];
   646	  for (const n of [...new Set(names)]) {
   647	    const p = join(repo, n);
   648	    units.push({ where: n, text: n, scope: "tree", kind: "path" });
   649	    if (!existsSync(p) && !lstatSync(p, { throwIfNoEntry: false })) {
   650	      // Deleted on disk, still in the index: the index copy is what a plain commit publishes.
   651	      try { units.push({ where: n, text: asText(git(repo, ["cat-file", "blob", `:${n}`])), scope: "tree", kind: "file" }); } catch { /* not in index either */ }
   652	      continue;
   653	    }
   654	    const s = lstatSync(p);
   655	    if (s.isSymbolicLink()) units.push({ where: `${n} (symlink target)`, text: readlinkSync(p), scope: "tree", kind: "file" });
   656	    else if (s.isFile()) units.push({ where: n, text: asText(readFileSync(p)), scope: "tree", kind: "file" });
   657	  }
   658	  return units;
   659	}

   662	export function revUnits(repo: string, rev: string): Unit[] {
   663	  // ⚠ Split at the FIRST tab only: a path may itself contain one (REVIEW-056 S2-3).
   664	  const entries = gitText(repo, ["ls-tree", "-r", "-z", "--full-tree", rev]).split("\0").filter(Boolean).map((l) => {
   665	    const t = l.indexOf("\t");
   666	    const [mode, type, sha] = l.slice(0, t).split(" ");
   667	    return { mode, type, sha, path: l.slice(t + 1) };
   668	  });
   669	  const gitlinks = entries.filter((e) => e.type === "commit").map((e) => e.path);
   670	  if (gitlinks.length) throw new Error(`a submodule at ${gitlinks.slice(0, 5).join(", ")}: its content is another repository and is not scanned`);
   671	  const blobs = entries.filter((e) => e.type === "blob");
   672	  const pathsOf = new Map<string, string[]>();
   673	  for (const e of blobs) pathsOf.set(e.sha, [...(pathsOf.get(e.sha) ?? []), e.path]);
   674	  const units: Unit[] = blobs.map((e) => ({ where: e.path, text: e.path, scope: "tree" as const, kind: "path" as const }));
   675	  for (const o of batchObjects(repo, [...pathsOf.keys()])) {
   676	    const ps = pathsOf.get(o.sha)!;
   677	    const text = asText(o.body);
   678	    if (ps.some((p) => p === ".gitattributes" || p.endsWith("/.gitattributes")) && /\bfilter\s*=|working-tree-encoding/.test(text)) {
   679	      throw new Error(`content-transforming attributes in ${ps.join(", ")} at ${rev}: the published bytes may not be the blobs`);
   680	    }
   681	    units.push({ where: ps.join("; "), text, scope: "tree", kind: "file", paths: ps.length });
   682	  }
   683	  return units;
   684	}

   686	/** A commit or tag message, without the identity and signature headers. */
   687	function messageOf(body: Uint8Array): string {
   688	  const t = asText(body);
   689	  const split = t.indexOf("\n\n");
   690	  const head = split === -1 ? t : t.slice(0, split);
   691	  const msg = split === -1 ? "" : t.slice(split + 2);
   692	  // Keep header lines that are not identity or signature: none carry free text
   693	  // except `encoding`, so only the message is returned.
   694	  void head;
   695	  return msg;
   696	}

   698	export function historyUnits(repo: string): Unit[] {
   699	  // ⚠ A shallow clone or a grafts file hides history from rev-list, so a pass
   700	  // over it would not be a pass over what the repository holds.
   701	  if (gitText(repo, ["rev-parse", "--is-shallow-repository"]).trim() === "true") throw new Error("the repository is shallow; history mode needs every commit");
   702	  const grafts = gitText(repo, ["rev-parse", "--git-path", "info/grafts"]).trim();
   703	  if (existsSync(join(repo, grafts)) || existsSync(grafts)) throw new Error(`a grafts file exists at ${grafts}; it rewrites what rev-list sees`);
   704	  const lines = gitText(repo, ["rev-list", "--objects", "--all"]).split("\n").filter(Boolean);
   705	  const pathOf = new Map<string, string>();
   706	  for (const l of lines) {
   707	    const sp = l.indexOf(" ");
   708	    const sha = sp === -1 ? l : l.slice(0, sp);
   709	    if (!pathOf.has(sha)) pathOf.set(sha, sp === -1 ? "" : l.slice(sp + 1));
   710	  }
   711	  const tags = gitText(repo, ["for-each-ref", "--format=%(objectname) %(objecttype)", "refs/tags"]).split("\n").filter((l) => l.endsWith(" tag")).map((l) => l.split(" ")[0]);
   712	  const units: Unit[] = [];
   713	  for (const o of batchObjects(repo, [...pathOf.keys(), ...tags])) {
   714	    const p = pathOf.get(o.sha) ?? "";
   715	    if (o.type === "blob") units.push({ where: `${p} @ blob ${o.sha.slice(0, 10)}`, text: asText(o.body), scope: "history", kind: "file" });
   716	    else if (o.type === "commit" || o.type === "tag") units.push({ where: `${o.type} ${o.sha.slice(0, 10)} message`, text: messageOf(o.body), scope: "history", kind: "message" });
   717	  }
   718	  // NUL-separated, because a path may contain a tab or a newline (REVIEW-056 S2-3).
   719	  const paths = new Set(gitText(repo, ["log", "--all", "-m", "--format=", "--name-only", "--no-renames", "-z"]).split("\0").filter(Boolean));
   720	  for (const p of paths) units.push({ where: `${p} (a path some commit touched)`, text: p, scope: "history", kind: "path" });
   721	  return units;
   722	}

   724	export interface Finding extends Hit { where: string; line: number; scope: "tree" | "history" }

   726	export function scanUnits(units: Unit[], store: Store): { findings: Finding[]; allowed: Map<string, number>; seenAllowed: Set<string> } {
   727	  const findings: Finding[] = [];
   728	  const allowed = new Map<string, number>();
   729	  const seenAllowed = new Set<string>();
   730	  for (const u of units) {
   731	    const hits = u.kind === "path" ? [secretFileHit(u.text), ...pathHits(u.text), ...emailHits(u.text)].filter((h): h is Hit => !!h) : scanText(u.text, store);
   732	    for (const h of hits) {
   733	      if (h.allowedBy) {
   734	        const k = `${h.cls}: ${h.allowedBy}`;
   735	        allowed.set(k, (allowed.get(k) ?? 0) + 1);
   736	        seenAllowed.add(h.allowedBy);
   737	        continue;
   738	      }
   739	      const line = u.kind === "path" ? 0 : u.text.slice(0, h.at).split("\n").length;
   740	      findings.push({ ...h, where: u.where, line, scope: u.scope });
   741	    }
   742	  }
   743	  return { findings, allowed, seenAllowed };
   744	}

  1052	export interface ScanResult { findings: Finding[]; allowed: Map<string, number>; seenAllowed: Set<string>; unitsTree: number; unitsHistory: number }
  1053	
  1054	export function scanRepo(repo: string, store: Store, o: { tree: boolean; history: boolean; rev?: string }): ScanResult {
  1055	  const t = o.tree ? (o.rev ? revUnits(repo, o.rev) : treeUnits(repo)) : [];
  1056	  const h = o.history ? historyUnits(repo) : [];
  1057	  const r = scanUnits([...t, ...h], store);
  1058	  // ⚠ Files are counted by PATH, not by unique blob (REVIEW-056 S5-3): two paths
  1059	  // with identical content are two published files.
  1060	  const files = (us: Unit[]) => us.filter((u) => u.kind === "file").reduce((n, u) => n + (u.paths ?? 1), 0);
  1061	  return { ...r, unitsTree: files(t), unitsHistory: h.filter((u) => u.kind !== "path").length };
  1062	}
  1063	
  1064	interface DecideIn { findings: Finding[]; store: Store; requireStore: boolean; strictHistory: boolean; unitsTree: number; unitsHistory: number; tree: boolean; history: boolean }
  1065	
  1066	export function decide(d: DecideIn): { exit: 0 | 1 | 2; word: string; failing: Finding[]; reported: Finding[]; why?: string } {
  1067	  if (d.requireStore && d.store.secrets === 0) return { exit: 2, word: "REFUSED", failing: [], reported: [], why: "no local secret store found; the known-value class cannot run (pass --no-local-store for the shape classes only)" };
  1068	  if (!d.tree && !d.history) return { exit: 2, word: "REFUSED", failing: [], reported: [], why: "nothing was selected to scan" };
  1069	  if ((d.tree && d.unitsTree === 0) || (d.history && d.unitsHistory === 0)) return { exit: 2, word: "REFUSED", failing: [], reported: [], why: "zero files scanned; an empty scan is not a pass" };
  1070	  const failing = d.findings.filter((f) => f.scope === "tree" || d.strictHistory || !PERSONAL.has(f.cls));

 function* batchObjects(repo: string, shas: string[]): Generator<{ sha: string; type: string; body: Uint8Array }> {
   if (!shas.length) return;
   const out = git(repo, ["cat-file", "--batch"], new TextEncoder().encode(shas.join("\n") + "\n"));
   let i = 0;
   const dec = new TextDecoder();
   while (i < out.length) {
     const nl = out.indexOf(10, i);
     const [sha, type, size] = dec.decode(out.subarray(i, nl)).split(" ");
     if (type === "missing") throw new Error(`object ${sha} missing`);
     const n = Number(size);
     yield { sha, type, body: out.subarray(nl + 1, nl + 1 + n) };
     i = nl + 1 + n + 1;
   }
 }
 
+/**
+ * ⚠ **Refuse what this gate cannot read as published** (`REVIEW-056` S2-1, S2-4).
+ * A `filter` attribute means `git add` stores bytes a clean filter produced, or,
+ * for Git LFS, a pointer while the content is published elsewhere. A
+ * `working-tree-encoding` attribute re-encodes on the way in. A gitlink or a
+ * nested repository publishes none of its content here. In each case the bytes
+ * on disk are not the bytes published, so the gate refuses rather than scanning
+ * the wrong ones. `git check-attr` reads `.gitattributes`, `.git/info/attributes`
+ * and `core.attributesFile` alike.

 /** A commit or tag message, without the identity and signature headers. */
 function messageOf(body: Uint8Array): string {
   const t = asText(body);
   const split = t.indexOf("\n\n");
   const head = split === -1 ? t : t.slice(0, split);
   const msg = split === -1 ? "" : t.slice(split + 2);
   // Keep header lines that are not identity or signature: none carry free text
   // except `encoding`, so only the message is returned.
   void head;
   return msg;
 }

 export interface Finding extends Hit { where: string; line: number; scope: "tree" | "history" }
 
 export function scanUnits(units: Unit[], store: Store): { findings: Finding[]; allowed: Map<string, number>; seenAllowed: Set<string> } {
   const findings: Finding[] = [];
   const allowed = new Map<string, number>();
   const seenAllowed = new Set<string>();
   for (const u of units) {
     const hits = u.kind === "path" ? [secretFileHit(u.text), ...pathHits(u.text), ...emailHits(u.text)].filter((h): h is Hit => !!h) : scanText(u.text, store);
     for (const h of hits) {
       if (h.allowedBy) {
         const k = `${h.cls}: ${h.allowedBy}`;
         allowed.set(k, (allowed.get(k) ?? 0) + 1);
         seenAllowed.add(h.allowedBy);
         continue;
       }
       const line = u.kind === "path" ? 0 : u.text.slice(0, h.at).split("\n").length;
       findings.push({ ...h, where: u.where, line, scope: u.scope });
     }
   }
   return { findings, allowed, seenAllowed };
 }

+import { mkdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
+import { join } from "node:path";
+import { randomBytes } from "node:crypto";
+import { encodeSeed } from "ripple-address-codec";
+
+const root = process.argv[2];
+const gate = "$USER_TMP/T/x.ROpM8B/repo/tools/check-no-secrets.ts";
+const env = { ...process.env, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: "1", GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: "/dev/null", GIT_AUTHOR_NAME: "probe", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL: "probe@example.invalid", GIT_COMMITTER_NAME: "probe", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL: "probe@example.invalid" };
+const sh = (cmd: string[], cwd = root) => {
+  const r = Bun.spawnSync(cmd, { cwd, env, stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
+  if (r.exitCode !== 0) throw new Error(`${cmd.join(" ")} (${r.exitCode}): ${new TextDecoder().decode(r.stderr)}`);
+  return new TextDecoder().decode(r.stdout).trim();
+};
+const git = (repo: string, ...args: string[]) => sh(["git", "-C", repo, ...args]);
+const init = (name: string) => { const p = join(root, name); mkdirSync(p, { recursive: true }); git(p, "init", "-q", "-b", "main"); return p; };
+const commit = (repo: string, msg = "probe") => { git(repo, "add", "-A"); git(repo, "commit", "-q", "--no-gpg-sign", "-m", msg); };
+const gateRun = (name: string, repo: string, args: string[]) => {
+  const r = Bun.spawnSync(["bun", "run", gate, "--repo", repo, ...args, "--no-local-store"], { cwd: repo, env, stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
+  const lines = new TextDecoder().decode(r.stdout).split("\n").filter((l) => /^(REFUSED:|FAILING:|scanned:|check-no-secrets:)/.test(l));
+  console.log(`${name}: process-exit=${r.exitCode}; ${lines.join(" | ")}`);
+};
+
+rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true });
+mkdirSync(root, { recursive: true });
+
+const filterEq = init("filter-equals");
+writeFileSync(join(filterEq, ".gitattributes"), "payload.txt filter=inject\n");
+writeFileSync(join(filterEq, "payload.txt"), "SAFE\n");
+gateRun("filter= tree", filterEq, ["--tree-only"]);
+commit(filterEq);
+gateRun("filter= rev", filterEq, ["--rev", "HEAD"]);
+
+const filterBare = init("filter-bare");
+git(filterBare, "config", "filter.set.clean", "sed 's/.*/SAFE/'");
+writeFileSync(join(filterBare, ".gitattributes"), "payload.txt filter\n");
+const filteredSeed = encodeSeed(randomBytes(16), "ed25519");
+writeFileSync(join(filterBare, "payload.txt"), `${filteredSeed}\n`);
+console.log(`bare filter check-attr: ${git(filterBare, "check-attr", "filter", "--", "payload.txt")}`);
+commit(filterBare);
+console.log(`bare filter committed payload: ${git(filterBare, "show", "HEAD:payload.txt")}`);
+gateRun("bare filter rev", filterBare, ["--rev", "HEAD"]);
+
+const attrComment = init("attr-comment");
+writeFileSync(join(attrComment, ".gitattributes"), "# Documentation example: *.txt filter=inject\n");
+writeFileSync(join(attrComment, "payload.txt"), "SAFE\n");
+commit(attrComment);
+console.log(`comment check-attr: ${git(attrComment, "check-attr", "filter", "--", "payload.txt")}`);
+gateRun("comment-only attribute rev", attrComment, ["--rev", "HEAD"]);
+
+const replace = init("replace");
+writeFileSync(join(replace, "f.txt"), `${encodeSeed(randomBytes(16), "ed25519")}\n`);
+commit(replace);
+const original = git(replace, "rev-parse", "HEAD:f.txt");
+writeFileSync(join(replace, "f.txt"), "SAFE\n");
+const safe = git(replace, "hash-object", "-w", "f.txt");
+git(replace, "replace", original, safe);
+gateRun("replace rev", replace, ["--rev", "HEAD"]);
+gateRun("replace history", replace, ["--history-only"]);
+
+const tab = init("tab");
+mkdirSync(join(tab, "a\tb"));
+writeFileSync(join(tab, "a\tb", "state.json"), "{}\n");
+commit(tab);
+gateRun("tab rev", tab, ["--rev", "HEAD"]);
+gateRun("tab history", tab, ["--history-only"]);
+
+const child = init("child");
+writeFileSync(join(child, "child.txt"), "SAFE\n");
+commit(child);
+const superRepo = init("ordinary-submodule");
+git(superRepo, "-c", "protocol.file.allow=always", "submodule", "add", "-q", child, "vendor/sub");
+commit(superRepo);
+gateRun("ordinary submodule tree", superRepo, ["--tree-only"]);
+gateRun("ordinary submodule rev", superRepo, ["--rev", "HEAD"]);
+
+const nested = init("nested");
+writeFileSync(join(nested, "top.txt"), "SAFE\n");
+const inner = join(nested, "inner");
+mkdirSync(inner);
+git(inner, "init", "-q", "-b", "main");
+writeFileSync(join(inner, "inside.txt"), "SAFE\n");
+gateRun("untracked nested tree", nested, ["--tree-only"]);
+
+const hist = init("history");
+writeFileSync(join(hist, "gone.txt"), `${encodeSeed(randomBytes(16), "secp256k1")}\n`);
+commit(hist, "secret old");
+rmSync(join(hist, "gone.txt"));
+commit(hist, "safe head");
+const head = git(hist, "rev-parse", "HEAD");
+const graftPath = git(hist, "rev-parse", "--git-path", "info/grafts");
+writeFileSync(join(hist, graftPath), `${head}\n`);
+gateRun("grafts history", hist, ["--history-only"]);
+rmSync(join(hist, graftPath));
+
+const shallow = join(root, "shallow");
+git(root, "clone", "-q", "--depth", "1", `file://${hist}`, shallow);
+gateRun("shallow history", shallow, ["--history-only"]);
+
+const dupes = init("dupes");
+writeFileSync(join(dupes, "a.txt"), "same\n");
+writeFileSync(join(dupes, "b.txt"), "same\n");
+commit(dupes);
+gateRun("duplicate blobs rev", dupes, ["--rev", "HEAD"]);

+import { mkdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
+import { join } from "node:path";
+import { randomBytes } from "node:crypto";
+import { encodeSeed } from "ripple-address-codec";
+
+const root = process.argv[2];
+const gate = "$USER_TMP/T/x.ROpM8B/repo/tools/check-no-secrets.ts";
+const env = { ...process.env, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: "1", GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: "/dev/null", GIT_AUTHOR_NAME: "probe", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL: "probe@example.invalid", GIT_COMMITTER_NAME: "probe", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL: "probe@example.invalid" };
+const sh = (cmd: string[], cwd = root) => {
+  const r = Bun.spawnSync(cmd, { cwd, env, stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
+  if (r.exitCode !== 0) throw new Error(`${cmd.join(" ")} (${r.exitCode}): ${new TextDecoder().decode(r.stderr)}`);
+  return new TextDecoder().decode(r.stdout).trim();
+};
+const git = (repo: string, ...args: string[]) => sh(["git", "-C", repo, ...args]);
+const init = (name: string) => { const p = join(root, name); mkdirSync(p, { recursive: true }); git(p, "init", "-q", "-b", "main"); return p; };
+const commit = (repo: string, msg = "probe") => { git(repo, "add", "-A"); git(repo, "commit", "-q", "--no-gpg-sign", "-m", msg); };
+const gateRun = (name: string, repo: string, args: string[]) => {
+  const r = Bun.spawnSync(["bun", "run", gate, "--repo", repo, ...args, "--no-local-store"], { cwd: repo, env, stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
+  const lines = new TextDecoder().decode(r.stdout).split("\n").filter((l) => /^(REFUSED:|FAILING:|scanned:|check-no-secrets:)/.test(l));
+  console.log(`${name}: process-exit=${r.exitCode}; ${lines.join(" | ")}`);
+};
+
+rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true });
+mkdirSync(root, { recursive: true });
+
+const filterEq = init("filter-equals");
+writeFileSync(join(filterEq, ".gitattributes"), "payload.txt filter=inject\n");
+writeFileSync(join(filterEq, "payload.txt"), "SAFE\n");
+gateRun("filter= tree", filterEq, ["--tree-only"]);
+commit(filterEq);
+gateRun("filter= rev", filterEq, ["--rev", "HEAD"]);
+
+const filterBare = init("filter-bare");
+git(filterBare, "config", "filter.set.clean", "sed 's/.*/SAFE/'");
+writeFileSync(join(filterBare, ".gitattributes"), "payload.txt filter\n");
+const filteredSeed = encodeSeed(randomBytes(16), "ed25519");
+writeFileSync(join(filterBare, "payload.txt"), `${filteredSeed}\n`);
+console.log(`bare filter check-attr: ${git(filterBare, "check-attr", "filter", "--", "payload.txt")}`);
+commit(filterBare);
+console.log(`bare filter committed payload: ${git(filterBare, "show", "HEAD:payload.txt")}`);
+gateRun("bare filter rev", filterBare, ["--rev", "HEAD"]);
+
+const attrComment = init("attr-comment");
+writeFileSync(join(attrComment, ".gitattributes"), "# Documentation example: *.txt filter=inject\n");
+writeFileSync(join(attrComment, "payload.txt"), "SAFE\n");
+commit(attrComment);
+console.log(`comment check-attr: ${git(attrComment, "check-attr", "filter", "--", "payload.txt")}`);
+gateRun("comment-only attribute rev", attrComment, ["--rev", "HEAD"]);
+
+const replace = init("replace");
+writeFileSync(join(replace, "f.txt"), `${encodeSeed(randomBytes(16), "ed25519")}\n`);
+commit(replace);
+const original = git(replace, "rev-parse", "HEAD:f.txt");
+writeFileSync(join(replace, "f.txt"), "SAFE\n");
+const safe = git(replace, "hash-object", "-w", "f.txt");
+git(replace, "replace", original, safe);
+gateRun("replace rev", replace, ["--rev", "HEAD"]);
+gateRun("replace history", replace, ["--history-only"]);
+
+const tab = init("tab");
+mkdirSync(join(tab, "a\tb"));
+writeFileSync(join(tab, "a\tb", "state.json"), "{}\n");
+commit(tab);
+gateRun("tab rev", tab, ["--rev", "HEAD"]);
+gateRun("tab history", tab, ["--history-only"]);
+
+const child = init("child");
+writeFileSync(join(child, "child.txt"), "SAFE\n");
+commit(child);
+const superRepo = init("ordinary-submodule");
+git(superRepo, "-c", "protocol.file.allow=always", "submodule", "add", "-q", child, "vendor/sub");
+commit(superRepo);
+gateRun("ordinary submodule tree", superRepo, ["--tree-only"]);
+gateRun("ordinary submodule rev", superRepo, ["--rev", "HEAD"]);
+
+const nested = init("nested");
+writeFileSync(join(nested, "top.txt"), "SAFE\n");

+git(inner, "init", "-q", "-b", "main");

+
+const hist = init("history");
+writeFileSync(join(hist, "gone.txt"), `${encodeSeed(randomBytes(16), "secp256k1")}\n`);
+commit(hist, "secret old");
+rmSync(join(hist, "gone.txt"));

+import { mkdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
+import { join } from "node:path";
+import { randomBytes } from "node:crypto";
+import { encodeSeed } from "ripple-address-codec";
+
+const root = process.argv[2];
+const gate = "$USER_TMP/T/x.ROpM8B/repo/tools/check-no-secrets.ts";
+const env = { ...process.env, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: "1", GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: "/dev/null", GIT_AUTHOR_NAME: "probe", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL: "probe@example.invalid", GIT_COMMITTER_NAME: "probe", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL: "probe@example.invalid" };
+const sh = (cmd: string[], cwd = root) => {
+  const r = Bun.spawnSync(cmd, { cwd, env, stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
+  if (r.exitCode !== 0) throw new Error(`${cmd.join(" ")} (${r.exitCode}): ${new TextDecoder().decode(r.stderr)}`);
+  return new TextDecoder().decode(r.stdout).trim();
+};
+const git = (repo: string, ...args: string[]) => sh(["git", "-C", repo, ...args]);
+const init = (name: string) => { const p = join(root, name); mkdirSync(p, { recursive: true }); git(p, "init", "-q", "-b", "main"); return p; };
+const commit = (repo: string, msg = "probe") => { git(repo, "add", "-A"); git(repo, "commit", "-q", "--no-gpg-sign", "-m", msg); };
+const gateRun = (name: string, repo: string, args: string[]) => {
+  const r = Bun.spawnSync(["bun", "run", gate, "--repo", repo, ...args, "--no-local-store"], { cwd: repo, env, stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
+  const lines = new TextDecoder().decode(r.stdout).split("\n").filter((l) => /^(REFUSED:|FAILING:|scanned:|check-no-secrets:)/.test(l));
+  console.log(`${name}: process-exit=${r.exitCode}; ${lines.join(" | ")}`);
+};
+
+rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true });
+mkdirSync(root, { recursive: true });
+
+const filterEq = init("filter-equals");
+writeFileSync(join(filterEq, ".gitattributes"), "payload.txt filter=inject\n");
+writeFileSync(join(filterEq, "payload.txt"), "SAFE\n");
+gateRun("filter= tree", filterEq, ["--tree-only"]);
+commit(filterEq);
+gateRun("filter= rev", filterEq, ["--rev", "HEAD"]);
+
+const filterBare = init("filter-bare");
+git(filterBare, "config", "filter.set.clean", "sed 's/.*/SAFE/'");
+writeFileSync(join(filterBare, ".gitattributes"), "payload.txt filter\n");
+const filteredSeed = encodeSeed(randomBytes(16), "ed25519");
+writeFileSync(join(filterBare, "payload.txt"), `${filteredSeed}\n`);
+console.log(`bare filter check-attr: ${git(filterBare, "check-attr", "filter", "--", "payload.txt")}`);
+commit(filterBare);
+console.log(`bare filter committed payload: ${git(filterBare, "show", "HEAD:payload.txt")}`);
+gateRun("bare filter rev", filterBare, ["--rev", "HEAD"]);
+
+const attrComment = init("attr-comment");
+writeFileSync(join(attrComment, ".gitattributes"), "# Documentation example: *.txt filter=inject\n");
+writeFileSync(join(attrComment, "payload.txt"), "SAFE\n");
+commit(attrComment);
+console.log(`comment check-attr: ${git(attrComment, "check-attr", "filter", "--", "payload.txt")}`);
+gateRun("comment-only attribute rev", attrComment, ["--rev", "HEAD"]);
+
+const replace = init("replace");
+writeFileSync(join(replace, "f.txt"), `${encodeSeed(randomBytes(16), "ed25519")}\n`);
+commit(replace);
+const original = git(replace, "rev-parse", "HEAD:f.txt");
+writeFileSync(join(replace, "f.txt"), "SAFE\n");
+const safe = git(replace, "hash-object", "-w", "f.txt");
+git(replace, "replace", original, safe);
+gateRun("replace rev", replace, ["--rev", "HEAD"]);
+gateRun("replace history", replace, ["--history-only"]);
+
+const tab = init("tab");
+mkdirSync(join(tab, "a\tb"));
+writeFileSync(join(tab, "a\tb", "state.json"), "{}\n");
+commit(tab);
+gateRun("tab rev", tab, ["--rev", "HEAD"]);
+gateRun("tab history", tab, ["--history-only"]);
+
+const child = init("child");
+writeFileSync(join(child, "child.txt"), "SAFE\n");
+commit(child);
+const superRepo = init("ordinary-submodule");
+git(superRepo, "-c", "protocol.file.allow=always", "submodule", "add", "-q", child, "vendor/sub");
+commit(superRepo);
+gateRun("ordinary submodule tree", superRepo, ["--tree-only"]);
+gateRun("ordinary submodule rev", superRepo, ["--rev", "HEAD"]);
+
+const nested = init("nested");
+writeFileSync(join(nested, "top.txt"), "SAFE\n");
+const inner = join(nested, "inner");
+mkdirSync(inner);
+git(inner, "init", "-q", "-b", "main");
+writeFileSync(join(inner, "inside.txt"), "SAFE\n");
+gateRun("untracked nested tree", nested, ["--tree-only"]);
+
+const hist = init("history");
+writeFileSync(join(hist, "gone.txt"), `${encodeSeed(randomBytes(16), "secp256k1")}\n`);
+commit(hist, "secret old");
+rmSync(join(hist, "gone.txt"));
+commit(hist, "safe head");
+const head = git(hist, "rev-parse", "HEAD");
+const graftPath = git(hist, "rev-parse", "--git-path", "info/grafts");
+writeFileSync(join(hist, graftPath), `${head}\n`);
+gateRun("grafts history", hist, ["--history-only"]);
+rmSync(join(hist, graftPath));
+
+const shallow = join(root, "shallow");
+git(root, "clone", "-q", "--depth", "1", `file://${hist}`, shallow);
+gateRun("shallow history", shallow, ["--history-only"]);
+
+const dupes = init("dupes");
+writeFileSync(join(dupes, "a.txt"), "same\n");
+writeFileSync(join(dupes, "b.txt"), "same\n");
+commit(dupes);
+gateRun("duplicate blobs rev", dupes, ["--rev", "HEAD"]);

+import { randomBytes } from "node:crypto";

+import { join } from "node:path";
+import { encodeSeed } from "ripple-address-codec";

+const result = (name: string, text: string) => {
+  const hits = scanText(text, empty);
+  console.log(`${name}: findings=${hits.filter((h) => !h.allowedBy).length} allowed=${hits.filter((h) => h.allowedBy).map((h) => h.allowedBy).join(" | ") || "none"}`);

+
